messages.subject: problem sampling from uniform(1,100) prior
parts:

Strangely, I am getting error when I use a uniform(1,100) prior (and no data), while getting expected results when my prior is uniform(-100,100)!

http://pastebin.com/McHMPZHq

The error is that all "proposals" are rejected, and getting the warnings listed below.

Hopefully, I did not do an embarrassing typo or something like that.

Thanks

messages.subject: Re: problem sampling from uniform(1,100) prior
parts:
parameters {
  real mu; // should be real<lower=1,upper=100> mu;
  real<lower=0> sig;
}
model {
  mu ~ uniform(1,100); // with above change, this line is not strictly necessary
  sig ~ inv_gamma(2,1);
}

Various bad things can happen when the prior puts zero mass on part of the support of a parameter.

Ben

messages.subject: Re: problem sampling from uniform(1,100) prior
parts:
If there is no prior on a parameter, it is considered uniform on its support. So, the real question is how to restrict the support of different elements of a matrix, and the answer unfortunately is that it is not as straightforward as one might hope. Marcus gave an example of doing so at this link:

https://groups.google.com/d/msg/stan-users/fZlVgP1xeU8/oPaUKlP2V2MJ

Ben

messages.subject: Re: problem sampling from uniform(1,100) prior
parts: On Sunday, September 30, 2012 3:25:05 PM UTC-4, tgs wrote:

Here is the real reason (above one just a simplified "boiled down" case): I want to put different priors on different elements of the matrix, unif(0,0.0001) on the upper triangular, unif(0,200) on diagonal, and unif(-200,200) on lower triangular elements.

http://pastebin.com/Xzh5rtjV

Or you can do something like

data {
  int<lower=1> K;
}
transformed data {
  int K_choose_2;
  K_choose_2 <- K * (K - 1) / 2;
}
parameters {
  real<lower=-200,upper=200> lowers[K_choose_2];
  real<lower=0,upper=0.001>  uppers[K_choose_2];
  real<lower=0,upper=200>     diagonals[K];
}
transformed parameters {
  matrix[K,K] mu;
  // for loops to put lowers, uppers, and diagonals into mu
}

Ben
